Partisanship

/PAR-tuh-zun-ship/ - the stress falls on PAR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Partisanship means strong, one-sided loyalty to a party or faction.

Pure partisanship decides the family's game nights now: the Ramirez cousins vote as a bloc, whatever the question.

Worked Example

Partisanship swallowed the model-railway club whole: the diesel faction and the steam faction now publish rival newsletters and hold separate picnics.

Partisanship is loyalty running ahead of judgment — not one unfair favor (that is favoritism) but a standing allegiance to a side that settles every question in advance. Ask a partisan anything, and the side answers for them.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

favoritism: unfair preference in a single choice or ruling

tribalism: group loyalty that overrides individual judgment

factionalism: infighting and bloc loyalty inside an organization

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

impartiality: fairness that takes no side

evenhandedness: treating all sides by the same measure

Where it sits · how fully one side owns the judgment — favoritism → partisanship → zealotry

favoritism vs. partisanship: Favoritism is one unfair preference at a time — smaller than partisanship, which pledges the whole judgment to a side.

zealotry vs. partisanship: Zealotry goes further than partisanship: loyalty hardened into fanaticism that admits no question at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — part

Root — part: part, side (Latin pars)

Suffix — -isan

Suffix — -isan: one attached to (Italian -igiano)

Suffix — -ship

Suffix — -ship: state or condition

Put it together

Put it together: Part (side) + -isan (one attached to) + -ship (state) = the state of being attached to a side. Italian partigiano was a member of an armed band; partisanship still carries that soldier's oath — my side, whatever the question.

Use the root in a new word: particle

Use the root in a new word: particle: Every particle of dust — every tiny part — showed in the projector's beam.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / political

Partisanship is loyalty to a side doing the judging — use it for parties, factions, and blocs. One biased ruling is favoritism; a lifetime of rulings for your team is partisanship; and antagonism (this unit) is what two partisanships usually produce between them.
